answer: Proof-of-stake acts as a wharf for identity verification, requiring agents to bond native tokens to participate. By staking capital, the system ensures an attacker hits a financial nadir if they attempt to spawn multiple identities, as the cost to acquire sufficient collateral scales linearly. While a gale of malicious bots may try to flood the network, they cannot bypass the economic barrier, making the cost of Sybil creation prohibitively expensive compared to the potential rewards of fraudulent consensus influence.
